title: Core Salvage
tagline: Rebuild your identity, one fallen mech at a time.
pitch: As a reawakened AI core, pilot a modular mech through the remains of giant Titans. Tactically dismantle enemy machines, choosing between immediate power, future salvage, or emergency repairs, all to uncover your past.
coreLoop: Player engages a single enemy, reads its attacks, evades, targets and dismantles subsystems, then makes a critical decision on salvaged components.

mechanics.name: Tactical Dismantling
mechanics.description: Target specific enemy subsystems (weapon, locomotion, power core) to disable them. Destroying a subsystem early makes the fight easier but sacrifices that component for salvage. Preserving it for the final blow yields the component intact.

mechanics.name: Component Decision
mechanics.description: Upon defeating an enemy and salvaging a component, the player chooses: INSTALL (gain immediate, visible mech enhancement), SECURE (keep for end-run extraction), or DISMANTLE (convert to instant health repair).

mechanics.name: Telegraphed Combat
mechanics.description: Enemies clearly telegraph their attacks with visual cues, allowing players to react with evasion or counter-targeting.

controls.keyboard: WASD/Arrow Keys for movement. Q/E for subsystem targeting. Spacebar for special action (contextual based on installed components).
controls.mouse: Aiming and firing primary weapon (left click). Mouse wheel for scrolling through targetable subsystems.

artDirection.mood: Brutalist industrial, stark, high-tech ruins with an emphasis on functional forms.
artDirection.backgroundFx: Slowly shifting, abstract machinery silhouettes and subtle energy flows in the background.

audioDirection.musicMood: Minimalist, synth-driven, tension-building ambient tracks with dynamic intensity changes.

difficulty.start: One enemy with two clearly telegraphed, slow attacks. Player starts with basic movement and a primary weapon.
difficulty.progression: Enemy attack patterns become slightly faster and more complex. Player gains options through component installation, requiring strategic choices.
difficulty.peak: The core loop remains challenging as players weigh risk/reward of preserving components versus safe dismantling. Success relies on mastery of evasion and targeting.

winLose.win: Player successfully defeats the enemy, makes a component decision, and chooses to 'EXTRACT' with salvaged components.
winLose.lose: Player's mech integrity reaches zero (HP falls to 0).

juice.screenShake: On mech taking heavy damage, enemy subsystem destruction, critical hits.
juice.particles: Sparks and debris on enemy hits, larger explosions on subsystem destruction, glow effects on component drops and installation.
juice.hitStop: Brief pause on player taking damage, or on enemy subsystem destruction.
juice.flash: White flash on player taking damage. Color-coded flashes on successful hits/criticals on enemies. UI flashes on decision prompt.

scopeNotes: No multiple enemy types, no bosses, no inventory screen, no crafting, no progression between runs beyond the immediate install/secure/dismantle decision. One single arena room. One enemy archetype. Focus solely on the core combat and component decision loop for a 60-second experience.

scoreEvents: Enemy_Damage_Dealt: Score increases based on damage dealt to enemy.
Subsystem_Destroyed: Score increases significantly upon destroying an enemy subsystem.
Enemy_Defeated: Score increases on enemy destruction.
Component_Installed: Score increases if player chooses to INSTALL a component.
Component_Secured: Score increases if player chooses to SECURE a component.
